meta_title: Compress Image to 100 KB Online, Free | Resize-It
meta_description: Compress a JPG, PNG or WebP image to under 100 KB for forms, email and websites. Good quality, measured results, no upload, no sign-up.
subtitle: Bring a photo under 100 KB for an application form, an email attachment or a web page, while keeping it sharp. Processed in your browser, never uploaded.

tool_workspace.description: Add one or more images; each is compressed to 100 KB or less.

requirements.intro: We compressed three 12-megapixel (3000 × 4000) phone photos to 100 KB with this tool:
requirements.notes_h3: Getting a good result at 100 KB
notes: Typical result: about 630–1100 px wide, sharp on phones and laptops and fine for most web pages.
For a website, consider WebP instead of JPEG: choose WebP as the output format for a smaller file at the same quality.
Crop first. If the form wants a face or a signature, crop away everything else (use the image cropper): fewer pixels to store means more detail in the part that matters.
We count 1 KB as 1000 bytes, so a "20 KB" file from this page is at most 20,000 bytes. That is also under the limit for forms that count 1 KB as 1024 bytes.
PNG files are converted to JPEG (or to WebP if they have transparency), because PNG cannot be compressed this far without losing its format.
If a form also asks for exact pixel dimensions (for example 200 × 230 px), resize to those dimensions first with the image resizer, then compress here.

how_to.title: How to compress an image to 100 KB
how_to.step1_text: Select or drag in a JPG, PNG or WebP image. It is processed in your browser and never uploaded.
how_to.step2_text: "To a file size" is already selected with 100 KB. Change the number if your form asks for something else.
how_to.step3_text: Click Compress Image. The tool finds the best quality that fits; if needed it also makes the image smaller in pixels and tells you the new size.
how_to.step4_text: The file downloads automatically and is 100 KB or less, so it fits forms that count 1 KB as 1000 or as 1024 bytes.

items.q: How do I reduce an image to 100 KB?
items.a: Add it on this page and click Compress Image. The 100 KB limit is already set, and the file downloads when it is ready.

items.q: How big can the photo stay at 100 KB?
items.a: In our tests a portrait stayed about 1000–1100 px wide and a very detailed landscape about 630 px. Simple, evenly lit photos keep more pixels.

items.q: Can I keep a PNG as PNG?
items.a: Not at this size. PNG is lossless and usually much bigger, so the tool saves JPEG, or WebP if the image has transparency.

items.q: Can I compress many images to 100 KB?
items.a: Yes. Add several and they download together as a ZIP, each one 100 KB or less.
No. Compression runs in your browser.
